label: The first spark
title: The first spark.
narrative: Long before formal science, our ancestors learned by watching, making, and trying again. A stone edge, a tended fire, and the returning seasons turned experience into knowledge that could be shared.

milestones.title: An edge, made by hand
milestones.description: Early toolmakers strike stone to produce sharp flakes, transforming natural materials into useful technologies.

milestones.title: Learning from fire
milestones.description: Evidence of ancient hearths reveals fire's growing role in cooking, protection, and social life; its earliest control remains an active research question.

milestones.title: Knowledge becomes collective
milestones.description: Making tools and gathering around hearths create opportunities to learn from one another and pass practical knowledge onward.

label: A world measured
title: A world measured.
narrative: Across Mesopotamia, Egypt, China, and the Mediterranean, observation takes written and mathematical form. Clay tablets and papyrus preserve ways to measure land, calculate quantities, and track the heavens beyond a single lifetime.

milestones.title: Mathematics on papyrus
milestones.description: Egypt's Rhind Mathematical Papyrus records practical arithmetic and geometry for problems of work and administration.

milestones.title: The sky, recorded
milestones.description: Babylonian astronomical tablets preserve systematic traditions of observing and organizing celestial phenomena.

milestones.title: Reasoning with calculation
milestones.description: Liu Hui comments on China's Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art, explaining methods used in surveying, trade, and engineering.

sources.title: University of St Andrews — Nine Chapters

label: Knowledge without borders
title: Knowledge without borders.
narrative: Indian mathematics and the scholarship of the Islamic world develop powerful new ways of calculating and investigating nature. Through translation, travel, and criticism, ideas cross languages and become the starting points for new discoveries.

milestones.title: Working with zero
milestones.description: In India, Brahmagupta gives rules for arithmetic involving zero and negative numbers in the Brahmasphutasiddhanta.

milestones.title: Algebra takes shape
milestones.description: Al-Khwarizmi's work in Baghdad sets out systematic methods for solving equations; its exact completion date is uncertain.

milestones.title: Light put to the test
milestones.description: Ibn al-Haytham combines mathematical reasoning with experiments to investigate vision and the behavior of light.

sources.title: University of St Andrews — Ibn al-Haytham

label: The scientific revolution
title: A new perspective.
narrative: New instruments and mathematical models challenge inherited pictures of the cosmos. Earth becomes a moving planet, and the same physical laws begin to connect a falling object with the orbit of a world.

milestones.title: Earth in motion
milestones.description: Copernicus publishes De revolutionibus, presenting a Sun-centered planetary system.

milestones.title: Moons around another world
milestones.description: Galileo's telescopic observations reveal moons orbiting Jupiter, challenging the idea that everything circles Earth.

milestones.title: One law for Earth and sky
milestones.description: Newton's Principia develops laws of motion and universal gravitation that explain planetary movement.

sources.title: University of Glasgow — Copernicus: De Revolutionibus

label: Forces of change
title: Forces of change.
narrative: Experiments reveal links between electricity and magnetism, opening the way to electric motors and generators. The study of living things also changes scale, as natural selection offers an explanation for how species change over generations.

milestones.title: Electricity becomes motion
milestones.description: Michael Faraday demonstrates electromagnetic rotation, an early step toward the electric motor.

milestones.title: Motion becomes electricity
milestones.description: Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction, establishing the principle behind electric generators.

milestones.title: Life through deep time
milestones.description: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species, developing natural selection after Wallace independently reaches a related explanation.

label: Beneath the visible
title: Beneath the visible.
narrative: Relativity and quantum physics overturn everyday intuitions about time, matter, and light. Inside living cells, X-ray evidence and molecular models reveal the double helix, connecting biological inheritance to physical structure.

milestones.title: Time is no longer absolute
milestones.description: Einstein's special relativity links measurements of space and time to the motion of the observer.

milestones.title: Gravity becomes geometry
milestones.description: Einstein's general relativity describes gravity through the curvature of spacetime.

milestones.title: A structure for inheritance
milestones.description: Watson and Crick propose DNA's double helix, informed by crucial X-ray work by Franklin, Gosling, Wilkins, and colleagues.

sources.title: King's College London — King's and DNA

label: The connected mind
title: The connected mind.
narrative: Computers and global networks change how knowledge is stored, shared, and discovered. Machine learning becomes a scientific instrument in its own right, finding useful patterns while leaving questions of understanding and reliability open.

milestones.title: Intelligence becomes a research field
milestones.description: The Dartmouth summer project brings researchers together around the newly named field of artificial intelligence.

milestones.title: Knowledge finds a web
milestones.description: At CERN, Tim Berners-Lee invents the World Wide Web to help researchers share information across computers.

milestones.title: AI enters the molecular world
milestones.description: AlphaFold's methodology and protein-structure database are released, giving researchers a new way to investigate biology.

sources.title: CERN — The birth of the Web
Dartmouth — The dawn of artificial intelligence

label: Beyond the human horizon
title: Beyond the human horizon.
narrative: What if our most powerful scientific tools became our most capable collaborators? Superintelligence could transform discovery, from medicine to new forms of energy. Its emergence and consequences remain uncertain; human choices would shape who benefits, and who remains in control.

milestones.title: A scientific partner
milestones.description: More capable systems could propose hypotheses, design experiments, and help researchers test new medicines, materials, and energy technologies.

milestones.title: Intelligence beyond our own
milestones.description: Superintelligence is a hypothetical threshold, not an established present capability or an inevitable next step.

milestones.title: Discovery with human purpose
milestones.description: In this imagined future, meaningful oversight, shared benefits, and the ability to correct or stop systems remain part of scientific progress.

sources.title: International AI Safety Report 2026 — capabilities, risks, and uncertainty
